step1_analysis.description: A passive differential attenuator using a cross-coupled NMOS switch network. It provides highly linear gain control by steering current between a straight path (fixed conductance) and a cross-coupled cancellation path (variable conductance), which is critical for achieving high IIP3 in the receiver's PGA.

paper_reference.title: 0.18-m CMOS Bluetooth Analog Receiver With 88-dBm Sensitivity

max_gain.description: Maximum differential voltage gain (when control voltage is 0V, cross path is OFF).

sky130_expected.calculation: Acts as a voltage divider of two equal NMOS resistors (XM8 and XM2). Gain = R_XM2 / (R_XM8 + R_XM2) = 0.5 = -6 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Since all NMOS switches have identical W/L (5u/0.5u) and gate voltage (1.8V), their ON resistances are equal, resulting in a perfect 1/2 voltage divider.

min_gain.description: Minimum differential voltage gain (when control voltage is VDD, cross path is fully ON).

sky130_expected.calculation: Cross path (XM9/XM10) perfectly cancels the straight path (XM8/XM4) since all have the same W/L and Vgs.
sky130_expected.reasoning: In a perfectly symmetric simulation, cancellation is nearly infinite, limited only by numerical precision.

sky130_expected.calculation: Limited by parasitic capacitances of the NMOS switches. R_on is ~270 ohm, C_p is ~10fF. BW = 1/(2*pi*R*C) > 10 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Passive switch networks in modern CMOS have extremely high intrinsic bandwidths, usually limited by the surrounding active stages rather than the switches themselves.

input_resistance.description: Differential input resistance at maximum gain.

sky130_expected.calculation: R_in = R_on(XM8) + R_on(XM2). R_on = 1 / (uCox * W/L * (Vgs - Vth)) = 1 / (270u * 10 * 1.38) = 270 ohms. Total = 540 ohms.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated using SKY130 NMOS parameters (unCox=270uA/V^2, Vth=0.42V).

step3_testbench.description: Measures the maximum gain, minimum gain, mid-point gain, bandwidth, and input resistance of the passive VGA by sweeping the control voltages.
